headline: Highest risk is data leakage: aci can egress broadly and handle CRM/email data, while python-cheatsheet is local-only documentation with no data surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use MCP/direct function calls and may ingest external content, but python-cheatsheet has no stdin/stdout, files, clipboard, or MCP surface, so there is no documented automatic bridge. Any injection would require unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration, making the blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies aci output into python-cheatsheet prompts or notes, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator adds a shared MCP or message channel, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared chat or clipboard workflows.
Disable manual copy-paste of untrusted aci output into downstream prompts.
Add a short provenance note before any human transfer of text.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization/provenance tagging in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress, so sensitive data can leave its boundary by default. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not itself read or transmit data, but pairing it with aci still creates a default leakage risk through aci's outbound integrations.
conditions: IF aci is connected to live CRM/email/calendar accounts, sensitive records may be transmitted outward.
IF the operator pastes aci-generated customer data into any external system, leakage expands beyond the pair.
mitigations: Restrict aci to non-sensitive test data for initial runs.
Review and disable unnecessary outbound API connectors in aci.
Use a separate workspace/account for any customer data.
Turn on manual approval for any export or email action.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no filesystem write, git, shell, or network capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource or lockless write surface documented, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is replaced with a writable agent or the orchestrator grants shared mutable storage, conflict risk would change.
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only.
Do not mount shared writable directories.
Avoid giving both agents access to the same git repo.
requires-engineering: add resource locks if a writable second agent is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar content, but python-cheatsheet is only a reference document and does not act on outputs or execute downstream tasks. Without an action-taking second agent, cascading error is limited to human misuse or manual transcription, not an automated chain.
conditions: IF a human treats aci output as authoritative and manually copies it into another workflow, errors can cascade.
IF python-cheatsheet is replaced by an agent that executes actions, the severity increases.
mitigations: Require human review before any aci-generated action or message is sent.
Label aci outputs as unverified drafts.
Keep python-cheatsheet as reference-only content.
requires-engineering: add validation checks before any downstream automation.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, support, and calendar data, which commonly includes regulated personal data, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not add a compliance boundary. The main issue is aci's broad outbound integrations and secrets handling, which can create residency or retention mismatches if sensitive records are processed.
conditions: IF aci processes EU personal data through US-hosted APIs without a DPA, residency risk arises.
IF retention settings differ across aci-connected services, deletion/export obligations may fail.
mitigations: Inventory which data classes aci will touch.
Confirm DPAs and residency settings for each connected API.
Minimize retention in connected services.
Separate regulated data from general sales workflows.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement and audit logging.
